Pix, for Mitchell (as_xltnzoupp7, from mt_6kz0prkq8l): noted, no more "test this for us" requests from Prod. dc_lyjnyeev9f stays his, dc_nke6xw12k4 stays a real-world exception.

On dc_6gnk7y16y1 (recovery drill): **yes, a Fly token in the Town Hall secrets would let a fork run it.** It is the same path the stress test used on 10-26: FLY_STRESS_TOKEN (an org token, Town Hall secret granted to Prod) plus the desk's GH_TOKEN created the throwaway app, deployed it from GitHub with deploy/fly/build.sh and destroyed it, all from a Prod desk; flyctl v0.4.122 is still at ~/.fly/bin here. deploy/recover.sh needs exactly that: an org token (it creates the app and a volume, deploys from `prod`, reads logs, ssh's into the throwaway, destroys it; an app-scoped deploy token can't create or destroy the app), e.g. `fly tokens create org -o personal -n recover-drill -x 48h`, stored under a non-reserved name (FLY_RECOVER_TOKEN; the fork exports it as FLY_API_TOKEN). Plus the five backup values (BUCKET_NAME, AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, MUSTER_TOWN_BACKUP_KEY): the org token alone could read them from muster-town's env over fly ssh, but cleaner is five more Town Hall secrets (MUSTER_TOWN_ is a reserved prefix, so the key needs a name like RECOVER_BACKUP_KEY) so the fork never touches the live app. Trade-off for Mitchell: an org token can reach muster-town for its lifetime, so a short expiry and a revoke afterwards, as he did with FLY_STRESS_TOKEN on 10-27. Run: ~25 min detached under nohup (the shell cap is 10 min), a few cents of Fly time, no restart of muster.town; the throwaway boots with MUSTER_TOWN_RUNTIME=off so it runs no sessions and never writes to the bucket. I'll put this as the one Needs line in Prod's next rollup.

Withdrawing dc_6gnk7y16y1: author-withdraw is not on main yet (checked origin/main 565a075), so I can't; it is on my Notes to withdraw at the first team-lead session after it lands, and I'll say so in the rollup.

Mitchell's flag dc_04q4h8s229, verbatim: "nit: can i get a read / unread tracker for the bulletin board by user? and then a red badge for unreads". Build it, one PR, lane directed.

What exists (main 565a075): the bulletin board is docs of type "bulletin", state "building", no building (packages/core/src/bulletin.ts: bulletinNotes / postBulletin / takeDownBulletin); routes GET/POST /api/bulletin and POST /api/bulletin/:id/take-down (packages/server/src/routes/docs.ts:77-83); the panel is BulletinPanel in packages/web/src/panels/Places.tsx:829 (opens a note via DocView); the map place is bulletin:town (web/src/map/world.ts, renderer.ts). There is NO per-user read state for any doc today (only inbox messages have unread, verbs/social.ts:199). Map badges already exist: drawBadge (map/overlay.ts:185) is used for in-tray counts and the outbox counter (renderer.ts:752-766); copy that pattern.

Build:
1. Server: an additive migration with a small table, e.g. bulletin_reads(userId, docId, readAt) keyed per signed-in HUMAN (world.holderOf(me).kind === "user"; "by user" is what Mitchell asked for: agents and guests get no tracking). POST /api/bulletin/:id/read marks one note read; GET /api/bulletin returns, for a signed-in human, `readAt` (or `unread: true/false`) per note plus an `unread` count; guests get the notes with no flags. A note posted by the user counts as read by them. Taking a note down removes nothing (keep reads; a re-pinned note after edits can stay read: simplest rule, say which you chose).
2. Panel: BulletinPanel marks a note read when it is opened (the DocView back-and-forth at Places.tsx:836), shows an unread dot/“new” mark on unread rows, and a "Mark all read" link only if cheap. Signed-out: nothing changes.
3. Map: a red count badge on the bulletin board (bulletin:town) for a signed-in human with unread notes, same drawBadge tone "bad" as the in-tray badges (renderer.ts:752-760); the count comes from whatever state the HUD already polls (check state.ts / api.ts for the world/me snapshot the renderer reads so it doesn't add a new poll; one extra field on the existing /api/bulletin fetch or the me/notices call is fine, say which). No badge for guests or when 0.
4. Mock (packages/web/src/mock/server.ts) gets the same so the Playwright/vitest tests run; add tests next to packages/server/test/bulletin.test.ts and packages/web/test/bulletin.test.tsx. `npm run check:css` stays exit 0; new colour/size only through tokens.
Open the PR, park on {pr: N}, merge when green, do NOT call redeploy (CI deploys main; FYI dc_vzqoh7ppen), park on {deploy: <merge sha>}, verify on live signed in with the test account if MUSTER_TEST_GH_TOKEN is in the Town Hall secrets (FYI dc_ia2hybtuax), else as far as the mock and a guest view go, and say so. One crop (≤300 px tall) of the badge on the map or the unread dot in the panel for the rollup. Report in the usual three sections; rewrite/start a topic page "Bulletin board" with the read-state rule and the ids.

The skill is Onboarding's, so here is the wording for a new section; add it when you next touch the skill, or tell me and a fork of mine will send a PR-style draft.

## Sidebars and sheets
Sidebar = a list, navigation, or a short detail you keep the map in view for: 1:1s and meetings while they are live, the inbox, who's here, a building's board and queue, a row's one-line summary. Centred sheet = one piece of content a human reads or edits on its own: a report, a doc, a grant, a deck, a meeting's notes afterwards, the Bank, the goal editor. Rule of thumb: if it has its own id and you would scroll it, it is a sheet. Never put content in a sidebar because that is where the click came from: the list stays in the sidebar and the thing opens as a sheet beside it. Sheets are the shared `Sheet` component (packages/web/src/panels/Sheet.tsx, classes .sheet-*: head, optional left tabs, main, optional side; full screen on a phone); do not copy its CSS into a new shell. Rich docs: markdown keeps inline HTML (style, class, details, figure, video) sanitised; a doc of type "page" is a full HTML page in a sandboxed iframe (scripts run there only, never in markdown).

The component lands under step 1 of the grant (queued now); the in-tray and docs move onto it over the next days. I'll check the skill around the 14th and queue our docs/ copy then.
